It had already become clear before the summer during the parliamentary inquiry into the coronavirus measures: the closure of schools during the coronavirus pandemic caused a great deal of harm to young people. According to clinical and developmental psychologist Bertus Jeronimus, this was quite simply the wrong decision.

Social media: swimming or drowning?
www.rug.nl/news/2026/08/0825-dijkstra
Date:24 August 2026

‘Smoking, online gambling, shooting heroin, nail biting. A daily glass of wine, as enjoyed by so many academics. Using social media. It’s all much the same,’ says Arie Dijkstra, Professor in the Social Psychology of Health and Illness, specializing in the psychology of health behaviour and addiction. ‘They are all types of behaviour that become disproportionately important to some people, at which point, behavioural psychology calls it addiction.’

UG at Noorderzon 2026

Date:17 August 2026

This summer, the RUG and the UMCG are again present at Noorderzon. Join discussions with scientists and attend interesting lectures.

Noorderzon “Festival of Performing Arts & Society” is one of the biggest festivals in the city of Groningen. This year, the festival takes place from 20 to 30 August.

Hubble solves merger mystery from Milky Way’s early years
www.rug.nl/news/2026/08/hubble-solves-merger-mystery-from-milky-way-s-early-years
Date:17 August 2026

Ten billion years ago, the Milky Way merged with a dwarf galaxy, as discovered in 2018 by a team led by University of Groningen astronomer Amina Helmi. Now, an international team of astronomers, including Helmi, has found evidence of an earlier merger that took place around 11.8 billion years ago.

InnoLaunch: Get your startup ready for takeoff in 8 weeks
www.rug.nl/news/2026/08/0811-innolaunch
Date:11 August 2026

What's stopping you from taking the first step in entrepreneurship? Is it because you think your idea isn't good enough? Or that you're simply not ready yet? You don't have to figure it all out on your own. InnoLaunch by business incubator Innokite is designed to help you take that first step.

Scientific research on the Dead Sea Scrolls: facts and context
www.rug.nl/news/2026/08/0807-dode-zee-rollen
Date:07 August 2026

The Dead Sea Scrolls, discovered between 1947 and 1965 in various caves, are among the most remarkable archaeological finds of the last century. These texts, primarily Jewish writings over 2,000 years old—including the oldest manuscripts of the Bible—were found in areas such as Qumran. At the time, these areas fell under different authorities: the British Mandate territory, Jordanian-occupied territory, and Israeli territory. No new Dead Sea Scrolls have been discovered since 1965.

CLDR takes next step: new sustainable laboratory building for UMCG and UG for care, research, and education
www.rug.nl/news/2026/08/260806-cldr-voorlopig-ontwerp
Date:06 August 2026

The UMCG and the University of Groningen (UG) are continuing the development of the new Central Laboratory for Diagnostics and Research (CLDR). In the coming period, the preliminary design will be further elaborated into a final design, bringing the realization of the new laboratory building one step closer.

Watch the solar eclipse on 12 August at one of the UG’s observation sites
www.rug.nl/news/2026/08/watch-the-solar-eclipse-on-12-august-at-one-of-the-ug-s-observation-sites
Date:05 August 2026

Europe is gearing up for a magnificent natural phenomenon: on 12 August, there will be a total solar eclipse in northern Spain. Here in the Netherlands, it will be a partial eclipse. No less than 90 per cent of the Sun will be obscured. The University of Groningen (UG) has set up observation points at various locations in the north, equipped with instruments and special eclipse glasses so that people can view the solar eclipse safely.
